$comment: OUTSTANDING: what a NEW materialize request would still have to ask for — requested, not
delivered, not permanently absent. The delivery-state document carries no status word, and
the derived STATE is not enough to act on: `Pending` is the wire shape of both 'the job row
is not visible yet' (wait, it will appear) and 'the run we joined has ended without building
this' (waiting is forever). A reader that cannot tell those apart polls out its whole budget
on the second — 5/6 = 83%, for ten minutes, with the platform long since finished.
`requested` below is the yardstick every vector is judged against, and is deliberately the
same set the deliveryVectors case uses so the two read together.

vectors.note: nothing left to ask for — the empty case, which is what Complete MEANS
a run in flight can still satisfy these, so outstanding is reported but is not yet a reason to ask again
a permanently-absent token is NOT outstanding — asking again for it buys nothing, and counting it would make a finished bundle poll forever

the seconds after a start: nothing delivered, no row visible yet. Outstanding is everything, and the right response is to WAIT — a reader must not read a non-empty outstanding as 'ask again' on its own

STOP: the run this host JOINED has ended without building everything the host needs. Byte-for-byte the same STATE as the vector above, and the difference is only knowable to a caller that has already SEEN a run in flight — which is why the response to this one is to ask again for exactly `outstanding`, and the response to the one above is to keep waiting. `lastAttempt.tokens` is EMPTY on purpose: the platform filters it to that run's own undelivered tokens, and the outstanding one was never in that run, so the Failed arms cannot rescue this. The Unreal importer had no re-pick and sat here at 5/6 = 83% for its whole ten-minute budget (2026-08-30).
